message.content:
The **first artificial satellite** was **Sputnik 1**, launched by the Soviet Union on **October 4, 1957**; it was about **58 cm** in diameter and weighed **83.6 kg**.[1][2] The **latest** widely recognized artificial satellites are much larger and more capable, but your query is too vague to identify a single “latest” satellite without a specific category or date range.

A quick comparison based on the sources provided:

| Feature | First satellite: Sputnik 1 | Later/early follow-up example: Explorer I |
|---|---|---|
| Launch date | October 4, 1957[1][2] | January 31, 1958[1][4] |
| Size | About 58 cm across[1] | Smaller/slighter than Sputnik[4] |
| Mass | 83.6 kg[1] | Smaller/slighter than Sputnik[4] |
| Purpose | Demonstrated the first artificial satellite in orbit[1][2] | Carried a scientific payload and discovered the Van Allen radiation belts[1] |

If you want, I can compare Sputnik 1 with the **most recent satellite in a specific class**—for example **communications**, **weather**, **GPS/navigation**, or **Earth observation**.
